issue.title: QGB-02: Obstacle Avoidance System — Test, Tune & Document

comments.body:
Hi @vector-arrow  , interested in contributing here, with a scoping question up front.
 Background: mechatronics/robotics engineering degree with ESP32/embedded experience, plus production Rust/C++ and systems engineering work. I've read through the OA system overview doc, the S2L driver PR, and the forum testing roadmap.

 Given that Phases 1–4 require physical access to the Quiver airframe and test sites (Texas open field, Germany tree-dense site), I don't think I'm positioned to run the physical flight testing end-to-end. But I'd like to offer help on the pieces that don't require hands-on airframe access:

 - **SITL-based parameter exploration** using the existing SF45-proxy simulation setup, to narrow the search space before physical tuning (if the SITL environment is accessible to non-core contributors)
 - **Analysis of existing flight logs** from the S2L dropout incidents, if any are available, to help characterize the vibration-resonance / connector / electrical-load hypotheses before committing test-flight time to each
 - **Documentation** — writing up the tuning process, parameter rationale, and final OA overview doc updates as the physical testing progresses

 If it's more useful to have one contributor own the whole bounty end-to-end including the physical testing, I understand , happy to step back or help in a supporting capacity instead. Let me know how you'd like to split this up, or if someone with local airframe access is already lined up.
